# `Q-22-8` — Math Macro Expansion Limit Exceeded

> Expanding the `\newcommand` macros in a math expression produced more tokens than the limit allows, which almost always means a macro refers to itself.

## What this means

Macros are expanded before the expression is converted. A definition such as `\newcommand{\loop}{\loop}` never stops expanding; TeX would hang, quarto-math stops after a fixed budget, reports the expression, and emits it verbatim in formats that need a conversion.

## Why this happens

Common causes: a macro that uses itself directly or through another macro, or a macro argument that reintroduces the macro.

## How to fix it

Remove the self-reference. If a legitimately large expansion hits the limit, split the expression or simplify the macros.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
